title: The hot lead
hook: Setty, sitting on a diner table next to the napkin dispenser, to the coach in the booth at 1 a.m., phone in hand behind a huge order: You let a [bleep]ing hot lead sleep on it, right?
biais: autorité (une étude, un chercheur nommé : Loewenstein, 2005)
écart de curiosité (« there's a name for it »)
pertinence pour soi (son lead chaud de la semaine, « tonight »)
ancrage dans le décor (il vit l'étude de la faim en direct)
caption:
Comment "SETTY" and he'll send you everything to build a free AI setter that books hot leads right in the DM. Follow so the DM lands 📩

👇 READ BELOW: what happens in a hot lead's head, from George Loewenstein's research on the hot-cold empathy gap.

1. In the DM, she feels it: "this is exactly what I need". She says she'll book tonight, and tonight never comes.

2. Psychologists call it the hot-cold empathy gap. When we're calm, we underestimate how much a strong feeling drives our choices, and in the moment we think we'll feel the same tomorrow (Loewenstein, 2005).

3. In one study, hungry people picked more junk food for next week than people who had just eaten (Read and van Leeuwen, 1998). It's a good way to read a lead who goes quiet overnight, along with plain old busy and forgot.

4. So finish in the DM while she's hot. Setty is the AI setter I built for coaches: through Manychat, he answers her last question in your voice, checks the fit, and offers two or three times in her time zone, right in the chat.

The catch: no study measured DM leads, so read this as a lens, not a law. Setty books on Cal.com, paid Calendly or iClosed, and with any other tool he sends your booking link. Building and testing him are free with no card, then going live starts a 14-day trial at $119/month per live setter.
